$comment: WHAT GITHUB STILL CALLS EACH SECRET, and why this file exists.
The migration gave every credential ONE name, spelled the same at the
workflow-env, Worker-binding, .env and Bitwarden layers. It could not give
it that name on GitHub: the operator ruled the GitHub-side rename skipped
(the org secrets are being deleted, not renamed), and `gh secret set`
cannot re-supply a value it is not allowed to read, so renaming there means
retyping 45 values by hand.
So `${{ secrets.X }}` -- and ONLY the right-hand side of that expression --
keeps the name GitHub holds. Everything else is the new name. This file is
the mapping, read by the gate rather than remembered.
IT COST A P0 TO LEARN. scripts/dev/secret-rename.py rewrote BOTH sides, so
267 expressions pointed at secrets that do not exist and evaluated to "":
every app-token mint, every R2 upload, both GPG signing steps and the whole
account deploy. GitHub does not error on an unknown secret, it substitutes
the empty string, which is why nothing said so. The tool now refuses to
rewrite a `secrets.` context (SECRETS_CTX), the same shape as its existing
`vars.` guard.
TWO NAMES ARE UNFIXABLE ON GITHUB, not merely unfixed. GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
and GITHUB_AUTOPILOT_PRIVATE_KEY can never be created: `gh secret set
GITHUB_ZZ_PROBE` returns `HTTP 422: Secret names must not start with
GITHUB_.` (probed 2026-09-02, nothing created -- the follow-up delete 404'd).
So those two are renamed at EVERY layer instead, to the names GitHub already
holds, and appear here as identity-free `renamed_away` entries.
THIS FILE IS SCAFFOLD. When the org secrets are deleted and jobs read
`${{ env.NAME }}` from Bitwarden instead, it is deleted with them, and
check_bws_map.py assertion 9 goes back to demanding an exact match.
The 3-to-1 collapse. There is ONE Stripe account -- the operator checked the
dashboard and ruled that STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_US and _ASIA are the SAME key as
EU (durable plan, decisions 8 and the 'Genuinely absent -- CORRECTED to ONE'
section). The unsuffixed value in the store is the EU one, by the same
ruling. So the pre-image is EU, not a per-region pick: the other two
spellings hold a duplicate of it and exist only because the old fan-in
demanded three names.
This is the ONE entry that asserts something about VALUES rather than names,
which is why it is written down here instead of being inferred at the call
site. If the ruling were wrong, a US or ASIA deploy would configure the
wrong live key -- so it is recorded, not assumed.
Reserved-prefix casualties. These are NOT pre-images: the new name is
illegal on GitHub, so the workflow layer uses the GitHub name at every
position and the store name is aliased at the request line
(`GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY > BWS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`).
